scope: Final visible Draft, exact source/article/action bytes, initial BookcaseDiscovery README and dynamic fleet discovery, the November 1 failure alert and repair chronology, ADR-0035 versus the actual alert job, PR #519 capture-time checks, existing Workstation reviews, and the article's explicit open-PR inventory. Read-only review; no article revision or acceptance, finding disposition, action admission or settlement, readiness, merge, workflow dispatch, runtime, or scheduling authority.

findings.title: The initial commit already states BookcaseDiscovery's purpose
findings.location: Lines 17 and 25 say purpose is unknown and will arrive when a README is authored.
findings.explanation: The initial commit already contains a README that describes phone-based live bookshelf-spine recognition and taste-based book discovery.
findings.correction: Report the initial README's stated purpose and keep only detailed architecture and fleet relationships explicitly unknown.

findings.title: The sweep is dynamic, not an authoritative static manifest
findings.location: Lines 17 and 25 use absence from a fleet manifest to classify the public repo.
findings.explanation: The pinned fleet contract derives sweep membership from the live GitHub org. Public repos remain swept when REPO_NOTES and prompt grounding are missing; that absence is surface drift, not exclusion from the fleet sweep.
findings.correction: Distinguish automatic sweep membership from missing role-note and prompt-grounding surfaces.

findings.title: PR 517 was the later fix, not a possible cause of the failed run
findings.location: Lines 31, 43 and 70 present a three-branch diagnosis with PR #517 as a possible regression.
findings.explanation: Run 41267355441 failed unit tests and skipped generation before PR #517 existed. PR #517 records job-scoped ACTION_REVIEW_DISABLED as the cause and moves it to generation-step scope as the repair.
findings.correction: Report the known test contamination and merged repair; do not make rediscovering it a prerequisite for unrelated editorial work.

findings.title: ADR 0035 does not define the pipeline-alert mechanism
findings.location: Line 31 attributes failed-run GitHub issues to ADR-0035.
findings.explanation: ADR-0035 is a Proposed status, auto-merge and feedback decision. The GitHub issue alert is defined directly in daily-blog.yml's alert-on-failure job and labeled roadmap A2.
findings.correction: Attribute the alert to the workflow's failure-alert job and its actual roadmap or decision source.

findings.title: PR 519 was blocked by a failing required check
findings.location: Lines 45 and 73 say #519 had no known blockers and was ready for a human merge decision.
findings.explanation: At capture, head 8d4d7b1 had a failed Test + pipeline smoke test because structured draft-candidate evidence binding was stale or foreign. Corrective commits and passing checks arrived on November 3.
findings.correction: Report the stale evidence-binding CI blocker and keep later repair and merge events outside this capture-time state.

findings.title: Workstation 8 through 10 already had structured reviews
findings.location: Lines 51, 70 and 71 propose scheduling reviews and recording findings for #8, #9 and #10.
findings.explanation: All three PRs already had substantive reviews submitted on October 30, with tests, ranked findings, scope limits, questions and explicit dispositions.
findings.correction: Start from the existing review findings and open decisions instead of proposing another generic review pass.

findings.title: The open and non-merge PR counts are understated
findings.location: Lines 45 through 59 enumerate the queue, then report 13 open PRs and 10 Draft or non-merge.
findings.explanation: The enumerated groups total 16 open PRs across six repos. Thirteen, not ten, were Draft or explicitly non-merge; the ordinary non-Draft PRs were #519, Morning Cockpit #60 and Classic Space #4.
findings.correction: Report 16 open PRs across six repos, 13 Draft or explicitly non-merge, and recalculate the queue interpretation.
